newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sets rules for exemption from new tax - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sets rules for exemption from new tax - paper.

text.p: The Brazilian government said only new quarterly savings accounts opened after January 25 will be exempt from Brazil's new 0.2-percent CPMF tax on all financial transactions, a local newspaper reported.

Folha de S. Paulo said the Central Bank refused to grant exemptions to normal accounts, stipulating that those seeking an exemption must open new 90-day savings accounts that earn on a quarterly basis.

The Brazilian government's economic team is slated to decide today if stock market transactions also will be exempt from the new so-called "check tax," although the decision is not likely to be announced until next week, it added.
Senior government officials have said the new tax, if levied on bolsa trade, will devastate the local markets by driving away foreign capital.
The government had said the new tax would take effect on January 23.
However, O Globo newspaper reported that Brasilia may now be levied starting sometime between January 25 and January 27.
